old: That he should resort to for these reasons: “I shall produce the heel-seizer, the reinforcer, the middle king or the neutral king; by any one of the neighbouring chief, forest chief, member of his family and prince in disfavour, I shall have his kingdom taken away or have [him] killed; or by supporting the party of the seducible I shall raise a revolt in his fort, country or camp; or by aupaniṣadika (upaniṣad-type) applications of weapon, fire and poison I shall kill [the one] near, as desired; or by an application of contrivance presided over by myself I shall bring him to loss and expenditure; or, in his group of allies or in [his] army, [when] afflicted by loss, expenditure and absence from home, I shall in due order obtain secret instigation; or by destruction of the supplies, reinforcements and foraging force I shall make a restraint of his camp; or, having raised a weak point by bringing up the army, I shall strike with the whole gathering; or, [his] energy struck back, I shall obtain peace as desired; or, of [one] bound to me, revolts will arise on all sides; or I shall have his base, [being] without reinforcement, destroyed by allies, forest tribes and armies; or, staying here, I shall protect the acquisition and security of a great region; my army, self-dispersed or dispersed by an ally, [standing] in one [place], will be unbearable for [me] staying here; or my army, skilled in battle on low ground, in excavations and at night, free from hindrance of the road, will do action in [the one] near; or [one] who has come here, [to an] unfavourable place and time, will not be, by himself indeed, through loss and expenditure; this region [is] one to be approached through great loss and expenditure, because of the abundance of forts, forests and places of retreat; for the others [it is] mostly disease, and [it is] one with ground not obtained for the exertions of armies; one fallen into adversity will enter it, or, having entered, will not come out.”

old: Lone '-' tokens at line ends are the e-text's continuation marks between the clauses of the quoted speech; the Hindi and English render them as clause breaks. The speech is the weak king's, addressed to the stronger king whose protection he seeks; 'tad' (n. acc.) has no clear referent (possibly the 'human fort' of unit 11, the strong king; or an adverb 'then/therefore'), rendered literally 'that'. Doubtful points: (1) pratipādayiṣyāmi (caus. prati-√pad) rendered 'produce' (glossary 3.11); the sense 'set up against him' is likely, the recipient is not stated. (2) aupaniṣadika = 'of the upaniṣad kind' (secret); praṇidhāna = application, placing; yoga-praṇidhāna rendered 'application of contrivance' (yoga as in 12.4), the sense could also be 'employment of agents'. (3) āsannam = 'the one near' (neighbour or one close by). (4) pratihata-utsāhena (instrumental) is taken as 'his energy struck back'; alternatively my own energy. (5) vadha rendered by 'destruction' for objects (supplies etc.), 'killing' possible. (6) daṇḍa-upanaya = bringing up the army; alternative: bringing him under force. sandhi: bare sandhi as the policy or its result is rendered 'peace' (glossary 7.3/7.4/7.8); 7.7 uses 'treaty' for its chapter, a person should align. Glossary conflicts: saṃśraya/yugya see units 8 and 21; sarva-sandoha = the whole gathering (7.4). (7) ihasthasya taken as genitive agreeing with the 'me' of me sainyam ('of [me] staying here'), ambiguous; ekastha = standing together in one place; aviṣahya = unbearable. (8) nimna-khāta-rātri-yuddha = battle on low ground, in pits, at night. (9) pathya-ābādha: pathya = of the road (also 'wholesome'); ābādha = hindrance. (10) 'kṣaya-vyayābhyāṃ na bhaviṣyati' literal 'will not be through loss and expenditure', probably 'will perish of itself'. (11) pareṣāṃ vyādhi-prāyaḥ sainya-vyāyāmānām alabdha-bhaumaḥ ca: nominatives taken as describing the region (ayaṃ deśaḥ): 'mostly disease for the others, and with ground not obtained for army exertions'; the exact sense of alabdha-bhauma is uncertain. The closing iti closes the quoted speech and is not rendered.
